evidence.full_prompt_before:
$$
\mathbf{f}(x,z)=⟨x,\hspace{0.222em}6{x}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}\text{___}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(x,z)$ above parametrizes the parabolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $y=6{x}^{2}.$ What is the third component of $\mathbf{f}?$
evidence.full_solution_before:
For any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{f}(x,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\hspace{0.222em}6{x}^{2},\hspace{0.222em}{\color{blue}z}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the third component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{blue}z}.$
evidence.independent_proof: F1(x,z)=(x,6x²,z) andF2(x,z)=(x,6x²,6z) both satisfy y=6x². Every(a,6a²,b) is F1(a,b)=F2(a,b/6), proving both surjective. Their tangent cross products(12x,−1,0) and(72x,−6,0) never vanish, proving both regular. Thus original unstated-convention bank had two valid parameterizations. Requiring the free parameter itself as the corresponding Cartesian coordinate selects z. z² excludes all negative third coordinates; x and6x² collapse the free axis (e.g neither reaches(0,0,1));6z fails only the now-explicit direct-coordinate requirement, and is not called an invalid general parameterization.
